Name two ancient devices used to measure time.
questions.a: Sundial (shadow clock) and water clock (also sand clock/hourglass).

questions.q: Why did people look for steady repeating events to measure time?
questions.a: Only regular events - like a swinging pendulum - give equal units of time.

questions.q: What device do we use today to measure time accurately?
questions.a: Clocks and watches (quartz and atomic clocks are the most accurate).

questions.q: When do we say an object is slow or fast?
questions.a: By comparing the distance covered in the same time - more distance means faster.

questions.q: What do we need to compare the motion of two objects?
questions.a: The distance each covers and the time taken - that is, their speeds.

questions.q: Which is faster: 60 km in 2 h or 45 km in 1 h?
questions.a: 45 km in 1 h (45 km/h beats 30 km/h).
Motion in a straight line with steady speed - equal distances in equal times.

questions.q: Give an example of non-uniform motion.
questions.a: A bus in city traffic, speeding up and stopping (or a falling leaf).

questions.q: What does the slope of a distance-time graph tell us?
questions.a: The speed - steeper slope means higher speed.
